Motor carrier interests favoring zone expansion. -Motor carrier interests espousing this position argue generally that our regulations should be updated to account for the migration of business and industry to the suburbs beyond the existing commercial zones and terminal areas which has occurred since the present regulations were adopted. These carriers believe that these shippers require the same responsive transportation services provided to shippers within the present zones. They assert that expansion will result in an increase in single line service, which will conserve fuel and eliminate delays and loss and damage claims. This should result in lower charges paid by the shipping public. Zone expansion would make motor carrier service available to small suburban shippers who do not have the volume, resources, or legal expertise to support an application for motor carrier authority, and it would spare carriers the expense involved in applying for new authority or purchasing operating rights.
